messages:
matt_support: Creating an escalation — customer BlueHarbor is stuck on provisioning step 2. Support got repeated `quota_exhausted` errors and timeout on agent provisioning. They can't proceed with onboarding. Adding CS for handoff and comms.

ops-bot: Ticket INC-91234 created by matt_support — priority: P1. Link: https://tickets.internal/INC-91234

sarah_csm: Thanks @matt_support. Heads up — BlueHarbor renewal window opens in 45 days. If onboarding stalls we risk churn. Need a quick comms plan + a timeline to share with customer. Can we get an engineering ETA? :worried:

joanne_cs_ops: On it. Proposed immediate plan: 1) Acknowledge to customer with transparent ETA (by EOD) 2) Offer a short-term workaround (provision on a dedicated pool) 3) Schedule a fix rollout + postmortem 4) Exec sync if we miss next milestone. Owners: joanne (customer comms), ricardo (eng), matt (support liaison).

ricardo_eng: Quick update after looking at logs — provisioning fails when internal quota check returns 502 from quota-service. Repro steps: 
```
POST /provision -> quota-service returns 502 -> handler times out at 30s -> rollback
```
I can deploy a hotfix to bypass the failing endpoint and fallback to cached quota checks. ETA for hotfix deploy: tomorrow 10:00 PT. If ops enables a temporary capacity bump we can short-circuit the need for fallback.

matt_support: Thanks @ricardo_eng. Can you also add a short blurb we can send to the customer explaining risk and workaround (non-technical)? I can push the temporary capacity bump if CS signs off.

sarah_csm: Please include: what happened, what we're doing to fix, expected timeline, and what customer can do (none — we handle it). I'll draft and send after you post the blurb. Also scheduling note: I'll book a 30m CTO call tomorrow 15:00 PT in case they want exec escalation.

ricardo_eng: Blurb draft (non-technical): "We're seeing an intermittent internal quota check error that prevents new provisioned agents from completing setup. We will apply a temporary capacity increase to get your onboarding back on track, then deploy a code fix to remove the intermittent failure. Expected restoration: tomorrow morning. We will follow up with a full incident summary." Feel free to edit.

joanne_cs_ops: Edited and fine — will send at 16:00 PT unless we have new info. Action items: 
- [ ] joanne: customer update (by 16:00 PT today)
- [ ] ricardo: hotfix deploy (tomorrow 10:00 PT)
- [ ] matt: enable temporary capacity bump and monitor (immediately after joanne says go)
- [ ] sarah: CTO call scheduled (tomorrow 15:00 PT)

matt_support: I created a temporary capacity request: REQ-3377. Waiting approval from infra team. If approved I'll flip the switch and post timestamps.

sarah_csm: Great — please cc me on the customer update. I'll capture this as a renewal-risk flag in the account (internal note).

ricardo_eng: If infra approval stalls, I can implement fallback in code and roll out through canary in ~3 hours after approval to start. But pref is infra bump for speed.

joanne_cs_ops: Customer-facing message ready. Sending now. I'll paste below and ping when sent.

joanne_cs_ops: "Hi BlueHarbor team — thanks for flagging this. We're currently seeing an intermittent quota check impacting provisioning. We're applying a temporary capacity increase to get your onboarding back online and will deploy a fix tomorrow morning. We'll follow up with confirmation when complete and a short incident summary. Apologies for the disruption — your onboarding is top priority. — Joanne, CS Ops"

matt_support: Infra approved REQ-3377 at 2024-11-05T18:15:00Z — enabling capacity now. Will monitor logs and report back in 15m.

ops-bot: Incident INC-91234 status updated: mitigation in progress (capacity bumped).

sarah_csm: Thanks team. I'll update renewal playbook and log the action items. If mitigation holds we'll plan a postmortem and then close the ticket.

matt_support: Monitoring shows successful provision attempts now. First two agents completed setup at 2024-11-05T18:22:11Z and 2024-11-05T18:25:03Z. Keeping thread updated.
